page0.text:
It's collapsing.
The collapse is all but assured.
The Einzberns' thousand-year quest.
The Makiris' five-hundred-year wish.
A world that has continued without ending, changing, or evolving is finally coming to an end.

page1.text:
"Oh... Oh, ohhhhhhh!!!"
Amidst the destruction, it still has a will.

page3.text:
Its body is nothing but a dark red lump of meat, looking nothing like a human.
It is a swarm of insects that dwelled in this cavern.
He gathered them all to form a single lump of flesh, but he cannot maintain a humanoid body anymore.

page4.text:
His writhing form is simply a lump of meat that can move.
But it's still alive.
The lump curses its rotting body and its melting soul.

page6.text: Only its obsession is still intact.

page7.text:
"Oooh... Ohhh, oh... OH..."
It crawls on the ground.
Zouken Makiri. The old mage, his main body anchoring his soul having been crushed, clings to this world by his obsession alone.
His doom is only a matter of time.
Although he has fit his soul into a hastily-assembled swarm of insects, he will never recover from being crushed twice.

page9.text:
The old mage who has become a lump of meat will die an agonizing death.
He will rot until the end, and die feeling regret.
It's right in front of him.
He gazes out at the embodiment of eternity which he sought for so long and was only one step away from obtaining.

page10.text: Are his death cries agony, or regret?

page12.text:
He doesn't want to die.
How can he just disappear now?
Five hundred years.
How can he disappear when the reward he deserves for five hundred agonizing years of effort is right before his eyes?

page13.text:
"Oh... Oh, ohhhhhhhh!"
All he remembers is suffering.
The karma of the Makiris.
They were a great magical house driven from their homeland, wandering until reaching this land in the Orient. Then, they were unable to assimilate to this land's laws and fell into decline.
But that wasn't true.
There would have still been hope if that was the case.
If that is why their bloodline died out, they might have gracefully accepted their demise.

page15.text:
But the truth was different.
It isn't that the land of Japan was unsuitable.
An external factor like that wouldn't have ended the Makiris.
They simply lost their way.

page16.text:
It has been three hundred years since the ancestral Makiri seekers.
In those three hundred years, they reached the limits of their lineage.
The Makiri mages were already in decline by Zouken's generation.
That is when the suffering began, and the old man had no choice but to deny it.
Zouken Matou's life was spent desperately trying to overcome the decline of the Makiri bloodline.

page17.text:
I don't want to die.
I don't want to die, I don't want to die...!

page18.text:
"Oh, oohh, OOOOOOOOOHHHH!!!"
Yes, I must not die. Damn this rotting body. It's painful, so painful. Too painful. Five hundred years of pain. My whole life has been pain. Why fault me for seeking eternity? I suffered and suffered, never fulfilled, so how can I disappear without leaving anything behind? How can I die in agony? The Holy Grail is open before me. So listen to my wish, ask and I shall answer. My wish is that I DON'T WANT TO DIE, I need to get there, my wish will come true if I climb that cliff, it'll grant my wish but I can't reach it with this body, it's so far away, these last five centuries have been for nothing, it's so far away, why oh why is it so far away—!?!?!?

page19.text:
He crawls, scattering and splattering his body.
What obsession.
He can't move, no, he shouldn't even have the ability to move, but his hatred drives it forward.

page20.text:
He is now an obsessive idea become a monster.
He doesn't hear the collapse. He only sees the Holy Grail as it moves forward.
And then, his misshapen form sees...
"...So you've changed this much, Makiri."
Someone with a beautiful, bell-like voice speaks to him.

page21.text:
"What...?"
He looks up.
In the middle of his wavering vision
stands a lone girl.

page22.text:
...
He stops.
He stares at her.
...The old mage does not see a girl.
He sees a woman from his distant memories.
The golden Einzbern woman who has never faded from his mind to this day.
Two hundred years ago...
She was his comrade—the Cup of Heaven who sacrificed herself to build the Greater Grail.

page23.text:
...
She hasn't changed at all since that day.
The woman of the Holy Grail looks at him with the same eyes as when he still burned with passion.
"Tell me, my nemesis. Why did you not want to die?"
She speaks just once, in a nostalgic voice.

page24.text:
...
Her question halts his thoughts of suffering.
Why?
Why?
Why?
It's strange, now that one asks.
Why did he not want to die?
Why couldn't he die?
He would be free from suffering in death, so for what purpose did he cling to life and suffering?

page26.text:
Yes, he had a noble goal at first.
He would acquire all of creation.
He would know all truths,
and reach lands nobody else could.
He would surpass the limits of the flesh and reach the limitlessness of the soul.

page27.text:
The human race.
He would let those saddled with limits from birth and forced to run circles within the spiral of their brains go outside.
To heal all hatred and suffering.

page28.text:
He remembers.
It was after the grief of learning that Paradise did not exist.
He excitedly decided that if it did not exist in this world and he was not allowed to create it while in a flesh body, then he would travel to a place where it was allowed.
Not to create a new world, but to turn himself, to turn the life called humanity into something new.

page29.text:
"Oh...ohh."
...That's right.
To go to the sky he always looked up at, and beyond.
He would be born anew in a place no one could imagine,
and arrive at a utopia we cannot visualize.

page30.text:
For that cause...
He sought the Holy Grail.
He sought a miracle beyond human reach.
He couldn't disappear until he attained it.
He knew he would suffer defeat and that he would not attain it in this body, but he never gave up as long as he lived.

page31.text:
Yes, he had just one dream.
The abolition of all the evil in the world.
We staked our lives on an impossible utopia.

page32.text:
"......Oh."
So he stayed behind.
After his enemies left, he kept searching, even as he knew it was pointless.
He believed that living itself had purpose, and knew that one day he would create someone to succeed him.

page33.text:
So he kept on living.
It was suffering, but he couldn't let himself die.
Even when he remade himself, he never overcame the laments of his youth.
Was that not his way of life, and the answer he arrived at?

page34.text:
...Yes.
Even if it lies beyond this life. Even if he isn't rewarded...

page35.text:
"Oh... Oohh, oh...!"
That was his first wish.
That agony.
How meager his wish to not die was, compared to his quest for an impossible dream...!

page36.text:
"...I see. It once was that way, Justeaze."
...He looks up at the world.
The cavern is already halfway to total collapse.
Sakura Matou has been liberated and taken from this world.
Aŋra Mainiiu, the birthed, completely flawed embodiment of the Third Magic is flickering like heat haze.
Finally...
the old mage accepts that he will never reach any of it.

page37.text:
"It's over.
My old wish, my agony, the Makiris' duty... it all ends here."
It was decided from the very beginning.
Wherever the Makiris' voyage ended would be their final resting place.

page38.text:
"Ha... Haha, hahaha."
And yet...
The end of their long suffering was not a wretched conclusion at all.

page39.text:
It has only just begun.
Their challenges and journeys have just begun.
Five hundred years is a trifle.
Far too short a time to accomplish anything.
What we desired was brilliant and precious, to be attained in the far future—
the maturation of humanity, whether it takes thousands or tens of thousands of years.

page40.text:
So this is but a trifling setback at the start of the journey, albeit a meaningful one.
Their wish is not over.
The journey begins now.
The history of their long, long journey to reach the great, great beyond begins its loop with the end of a dream.

page41.text:
"...But it's too bad. I really was just one step away."
The words of resignation belong to the old mage after all.
No matter how brilliant his objective, he is a fiend who approves of wicked deeds.
He never overcame that trait even at the end, and cut his obsession with life.

page42.text:
The last one disappears.
One of the mages sought a miracle, an observer who was there at the very beginning, crumbles away.

page43.text:
"Five hundred years... Heh. That wish went by in the blink of an eye."
The lump of meat is swallowed by the rubble, leaving no trace.

page44.text:
He was a creature which lived while transforming.
The old mage completely disappears from the world, along with the fall of his long-sought wish.
